stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: 10 June 2026 strike
frames.note: The story begins with the US strike in the Gulf of Oman that killed Indian seafarers aboard a tanker. Under this frame the situation reads as a sovereignty and accountability question: foreign nationals killed in international waters, families asking how the rescue was handled, and a foreign minister raising the deaths directly with Washington. New Delhi, the family of the Himachal sailor, and Indian outlets open here.

frames.label: 13 June 2025 12-Day War
frames.note: The story begins one year earlier with the opening of the 12-Day War between the US, Israel and Iran. Under this frame the tanker strike reads as another chapter of an ongoing armed conflict, with the anniversary, Khamenei's funeral and continuing strikes on Lebanon framing the incident as wartime, not enforcement. Tehran, Press TV and Iranian officials open with this anniversary date.

frames.label: May 2018 sanctions snapback
frames.note: The story begins with the US exit from the Iran nuclear deal and the snapback of sanctions on Iranian oil exports. Under this frame the tanker strike reads as enforcement of a long-running sanctions regime against suspected smuggling through Hormuz, with Secretary Rubio saying Hormuz violations will not be tolerated. Washington and US officials open here.

bands.label: Strike and deal scramble
bands.summary: A US strike in the Gulf of Oman kills Indian sailors as Trump announces a US-Iran deal to be signed and the Strait of Hormuz set to reopen, with Iranian officials publicly contradicting the timing.

nodes.title: US strike in Gulf of Oman kills Indian seafarers on tanker
nodes.what: A US military strike on a tanker in the Gulf of Oman killed Indian crew members, including a sailor from Himachal Pradesh. Indian media reported that the family of the dead seafarer pressed for an inquiry and questioned how the rescue was handled. The strike set the stage for diplomatic exchanges between New Delhi and Washington in the days that followed.

cites.l: New Indian Express - Himachal sailor family

nodes.title: Jaishankar raises seafarer deaths with US; Rubio cites Hormuz enforcement
nodes.what: Indian External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar raised the killing of Indian seafarers directly with Washington. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in public remarks that violations in the Strait of Hormuz would not be tolerated, framing US action in the waterway as enforcement against suspected smuggling. Indian outlets and CubaHeadlines reported the exchange as New Delhi demanding accountability from the United States.

cites.l: New Indian Express - Rubio and Jaishankar

nodes.title: Trump announces US-Iran deal to be signed Sunday with Hormuz to reopen
nodes.what: US President Donald Trump said a US-Iran agreement would be signed on Sunday, June 14, and that the Strait of Hormuz would open shortly after. The BBC, Guardian and TASS carried the announcement, with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also saying a memorandum was expected within 24 hours.

cites.l: TASS - Trump on June 14 deal and Hormuz

nodes.disputed: Trump and Pakistani PM Sharif describe the signing as set for Sunday June 14; Iran's Foreign Ministry, cited by TASS and Al Jazeera, says no peace memorandum will be signed on Sunday.

nodes.title: Israel strikes southern Lebanon as Washington says deal is near
nodes.what: Israel carried out air strikes on southern Lebanon on the same day US officials said a deal with Iran was imminent. Al Jazeera and Anadolu reported that Israeli media described the strikes as continuing despite the diplomatic track, and that Israel would not withdraw from southern Lebanon under the US-Iran understandings.

nodes.title: Iran marks first anniversary of the 12-Day War and sets Khamenei funeral
nodes.what: Iranian officials marked one year since the start of the June 2025 12-Day War with the United States and Israel. State broadcaster Press TV carried statements that 'justice will be served' over the events of June 2025. Iranian authorities also announced funeral and burial dates for the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

nodes.title: Iran says deal to end the war will not be signed today
nodes.what: Iranian officials publicly stated that the agreement Trump had announced for Sunday would not be signed that day, as reported by the Taipei Times. TASS, citing Axios, had earlier described a planned virtual signing of a memorandum, while other reports said US and Iranian representatives might instead meet in Switzerland the following week.

cites.l: Taipei Times - Iran says no signing today

bands.label: After the 12-Day War
bands.summary: The June 2025 12-Day War between the US, Israel and Iran reshapes the region, with the death of Supreme Leader Khamenei, continued Israeli strikes on Lebanon, and a year of stalled negotiations leading into the anniversary.

nodes.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon resume at scale
nodes.what: Israel carried out an expanded wave of strikes on Hezbollah positions and infrastructure in southern Lebanon and the Bekaa, citing rearmament in violation of the November 2024 ceasefire. Lebanese authorities reported civilian casualties and damage across multiple villages.

nodes.title: US-Iran talks stall ahead of war anniversary
nodes.what: Indirect US-Iran negotiations on a successor nuclear and sanctions framework reached an impasse, with disputes over enrichment ceilings and sanctions relief. Both sides issued public statements blaming the other as the first anniversary of the 12-Day War approached.
nodes.disputed: US officials described Iran as refusing verifiable limits on enrichment; Iranian officials described Washington as demanding concessions beyond the original 2015 framework.

bands.label: Maximum pressure era
bands.summary: Washington exits the nuclear deal and reimposes sanctions on Iranian oil, building up a Hormuz enforcement posture with recurring tanker seizures and incidents through the late 2010s and early 2020s.

nodes.title: Tankers Kokuka Courageous and Front Altair damaged in Gulf of Oman
nodes.what: Two tankers were struck near the Strait of Hormuz, forcing crews to abandon ship and prompting international rescue. The incident came weeks after similar attacks off Fujairah in May and pushed US and Iranian forces into a public standoff over Hormuz transit. It became a defining episode of the maximum pressure period.
nodes.disputed: US Central Command described the attacks as Iranian limpet mine operations and released video purporting to show an IRGC boat removing an unexploded device; Iran rejected the allegation and described the US account as fabricated to justify escalation.

nodes.title: US drone strike kills IRGC Quds commander Qasem Soleimani in Baghdad
nodes.what: A US strike at Baghdad airport killed Major General Qasem Soleimani and Iraqi militia leader Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis. Iran responded days later with ballistic missile strikes on the Al Asad airbase in Iraq. In the same hours Iranian air defences shot down Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 near Tehran, killing all aboard.

nodes.title: Iran launches direct missile and drone strike on Israel
nodes.what: Iran fired more than 300 drones and missiles at Israel in retaliation for a strike on its consular compound in Damascus, marking the first direct Iranian attack from its own territory on Israeli soil. Most projectiles were intercepted by Israeli, US, UK and Jordanian forces. A second Iranian direct salvo followed in October 2024.

nodes.title: Trump signs memo restoring maximum pressure on Iran
nodes.what: Returning to office, President Trump signed a National Security Presidential Memorandum directing the Treasury and State Departments to drive Iran's oil exports to zero and to deny Tehran any path to a nuclear weapon. The order revived the sanctions architecture that had defined his first term and set the stage for renewed Hormuz enforcement.
